messages:
alex: quick heads-up — planning an infra apply during the release window at 09:30 PT. target: tenant-network + natgw routing. i want a dry-run + a short rollback playbook review before we hit prod.
maria: ack. are we pinning provider versions this run? last week drifted on provider bump.
kevin: yes pin to `hashicorp/aws` 4.62.0 for this apply. also recommend serial apply for route changes to avoid flapping.
sam: checklist i'll follow: backup tfstate, snapshot NAT instances, run tf plan + preserve plan output, mark canary tenants, standby oncall.
alex: copying checklist to release notes. draft rollback playbook below — please sanity-check: 
```
1) abort deploybot run if errors > 3 in plan/apply
2) restore tfstate snapshot: s-tenantnet-2026-03-21-001
3) remove route-table entries added in this run
4) if IAM changes fail, revert service-account bindings and rotate affected keys
5) escalate to network lead if BGP peers >2 down
```
maria: minor tweak: add step 0 = take provider plugin snapshot and publish to release artifacts. and notify security about IAM revert path.
kevin: add monitoring thresholds: BGP peer down >120s, route convergence >90s, control-plane 5xx rate >0.5% -> trigger rollback.
deploybot: [deploybot] dry-run scheduled: run id 83421. to cancel: `deploybot cancel 83421`. plan will be posted to #eng-infra.
alex: starting dry-run now. tagging run with `release/2026-03-21` and `serial=true`. canary count = 2.
deploybot: dry-run complete. plan shows 8 creates, 3 updates, 1 replace. important: one update touches `aws_iam_policy_attachment` for svc-account-analytics. plan file: https://internal.corp/release/plans/83421.plan
sam: scanning plan — IAM update looks additive but double-check bindings for cross-account role. will flag if risky.
ops-oncall: i'm on call for the window. i'll watch auth errors and BGP metrics. page me on PagerDuty if thresholds tripped.
maria: looks ok for canary A. proceed with canary A apply (tenant-a).
kevin: run canary A in serial mode, wait 10 minutes, collect net-metrics + auth logs.
alex: canary A applied, no observed regressions in 12m. proceeding to canary B.
ops-oncall: seeing auth spikes for tenant-b at minute 4: ~0.8% 5xx on token exchange. rolling back canary B now and halting main rollout.
sam: aborting remaining batches. starting rollback steps: restoring tfstate snapshot s-tenantnet-2026-03-21-001, removing route changes from tenant-b, reverting IAM attachments.
deploybot: run 83421 aborted by @sam. rollback job 83422 created and executed.
deploybot: rollback complete. tfstate restored to s-tenantnet-2026-03-21-001. changes reverted.
alex: confirmed rollback applied. thanks @ops-oncall for spotting auth spike. i'll update release notes to mark rollback and list mitigations.
maria: file a short incident note in #incidents and assign postmortem owner. we should add an automated canary rollback trigger in deploy pipeline for auth spikes.
kevin: agreed — add a preflight canary monitor step to auto-abort on auth error rate >0.5%.
alex: created postmortem stub and added follow-ups to the release checklist. TL;DR: dry-run caught potential instability but canary revealed issue; rollback path worked as expected. thanks all :thumbsup:
